tasks.title: Family cooking challenge
tasks.instruction: You must answer this question. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.subject: Family cooking challenge – your ideas
paragraphs: As you know, our class is helping to plan a family cooking challenge. We want to encourage families to cook healthy meals together. I need your help to decide on a few things.
First, should the challenge focus on cooking with fresh vegetables or on using less sugar? Which do you think is more important for healthy cooking?
Also, we need to choose one practical consequence to consider. For example, some families may find it hard to get fresh vegetables in winter. What do you think is a possible problem?
Finally, can you suggest one way to help families keep cooking healthily after the challenge ends?

promptBlocks.heading: Notes for your reply
listItems: Say which focus you prefer (fresh vegetables or less sugar) and explain why.
Describe one practical problem families might face and suggest a solution.
Suggest one way to encourage healthy cooking after the challenge.
Ask Mrs Hill about the date of the challenge.

promptBlocks.text: Write your email to Mrs Hill using all the notes.

tasks.title: Healthy cooking article
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.heading: Articles wanted!
paragraphs: Our specialist magazine wants to hear about your experience with the family cooking challenge.
What is the most important thing families should learn about healthy cooking?
How can the challenge help families eat better in the long term?
Would you recommend the challenge to other families? Why?
Write an article answering these questions and we will put it on our website!

tasks.title: Cooking challenge story
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.text: Your English teacher has asked you to write a story.
Your story must begin with this sentence:
"When the programme coordinator announced that the cooking challenge would start next week, my family looked at each other nervously."

designReview.specificSetting: a family cooking challenge planning brief 34

tasks.scenario: Student helps plan a family cooking challenge by emailing the teacher about focus, a practical problem, and post-challenge support.
tasks.purpose: Evaluate and justify priorities for the challenge (fresh vegetables vs less sugar), describe a problem and solution, suggest a way to sustain healthy cooking, and ask about the date.
requiredContentPoints: the main healthy cooking issue (focus on fresh vegetables or less sugar)
one practical consequence (a problem families might face)
a justified recommendation (way to encourage healthy cooking after challenge)
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Scenario is a family cooking challenge planning brief, not used in any previous test. Email structure with four notes is original. No overlap with forbidden concepts.

tasks.scenario: Student writes an article for a specialist magazine about the family cooking challenge, explaining key learning, long-term benefits, and recommendation.
tasks.purpose: Assess effectiveness of the challenge and recommend it to others.
requiredContentPoints: the main healthy cooking issue (most important thing families should learn)
one practical consequence (how challenge helps long-term eating)
a justified recommendation (whether to recommend to other families)
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Article genre with three direct questions about the challenge. Not a reused frame from previous tests. No forbidden concepts.

tasks.scenario: Student writes a story beginning with a sentence about the family's nervous reaction to the cooking challenge announcement.
tasks.purpose: Analyse implications and propose action through narrative.
requiredContentPoints: the main healthy cooking issue (family's nervousness about challenge)
a justified recommendation (implied through story resolution)
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Story opening is unique and matches the specific setting. Not similar to any previous story opening. No forbidden concepts.

designReview.overallOriginalityCheck: All tasks are built around the specific setting 'a family cooking challenge planning brief 34'. No overlap with existing test fingerprints. Forbidden concepts avoided.
